subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which cardinal and Lord Chancellor fell from power after failing to secure Henry's divorce?
questions.explain: Cardinal Wolsey fell from power in 1529 after failing to obtain the annulment from the Pope.

questions.q: What policy, begun in 1536, saw monasteries closed and their wealth taken by the Crown?
questions.explain: The Dissolution of the Monasteries (from 1536) closed religious houses and transferred their wealth to Henry.

questions.q: Which wife gave Henry VIII his long-awaited male heir, the future Edward VI?
questions.explain: Jane Seymour gave birth to Edward VI in 1537 but died shortly afterwards.

questions.q: The Pilgrimage of Grace of 1536 was a rebellion against which policy?
options: Religious changes including the dissolution of monasteries
questions.explain: The Pilgrimage of Grace was a northern rising against Henry's religious reforms, especially the dissolution.

questions.q: Who replaced Wolsey as Henry VIII's chief minister and organised the break with Rome?
questions.explain: Thomas Cromwell rose to become Henry's chief minister and engineered the break with Rome.

questions.q: Anne Boleyn, Henry's second wife, met what fate in 1536?
questions.explain: Anne Boleyn was executed in 1536 on charges of adultery and treason.

questions.q: Who was Henry VIII's first wife, whom he sought to divorce?
questions.explain: Catherine of Aragon was Henry's first wife; his attempt to annul their marriage began the 'Great Matter'.

questions.q: Sir Thomas More was executed in 1535 for refusing to do what?
options: Accept Henry as Supreme Head of the Church
questions.explain: Thomas More was executed for refusing to swear the oath accepting Henry's supremacy over the Church.

questions.q: What did the Act of Supremacy of 1534 declare Henry VIII to be?
options: Supreme Head of the Church of England
questions.explain: The 1534 Act declared Henry the Supreme Head of the Church of England, breaking from Rome.

options: His attempt to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon
questions.explain: The 'Great Matter' was Henry's drawn-out effort to end his first marriage so he could marry Anne Boleyn.

questions.q: The Act of Supremacy, making Henry head of the Church in England, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Act of Supremacy of 1534 made Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England.

questions.q: In which year did Henry VIII become King of England?
questions.explain: Henry VIII succeeded his father Henry VII in 1509.
